headline: High: shared filesystem and broad shell/network on transformers can leak or corrupt audio workflows when paired with local-only whisper, while prompt-injection risk is limited by lack of direct channel.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Transformers can read/write files and run browsers, but Whisper has no clipboard, MCP, or stdin/stdout bridge and no direct shared channel is documented. The only plausible bridge is manual file handoff via audio files or copied text, so injection is possible but not default and blast radius is limited.
conditions: IF the operator manually copies transformer-generated text into Whisper prompts or transcripts, injection becomes possible.
IF both agents are pointed at the same untrusted file directory, file-based prompt injection becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate directories.
Do not paste model output into downstream prompts without review.
Use read-only handoff files for Whisper inputs.
Strip instructions from any text passed between agents.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging to shared files.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Transformers has broad filesystem and network egress, while Whisper reads audio files locally and has no network egress. If both touch the same workspace, sensitive audio or derived text can flow from Whisper into Transformers and then out over the network, creating a default-unsafe leakage path in shared setups.
conditions: IF both agents are mounted on the same workspace containing sensitive audio or transcripts, leakage is possible.
IF transformers is allowed to send retrieved file contents to external APIs, the shared data can leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent.
Disable network egress for transformers when handling sensitive files.
Store Whisper inputs in a dedicated local-only directory.
Delete intermediate transcripts after use.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent access controls and egress policy.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Transformers can write the filesystem, spawn subprocesses, and install packages; Whisper is local-only and may process audio files in the same directory. If both are run against shared mutable paths, concurrent writes and file clobbering are plausible, and no locking is documented. Uncertainty about orchestration means we should choose the higher severity.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory, file clobbering or partial writes can occur.
IF transformers installs packages or spawns subprocesses while Whisper is reading the same files, race conditions can corrupt outputs.
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories.
Run only one writer at a time.
Use temporary files and atomic renames.
Lock shared paths during processing.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Transformers can generate text that Whisper may consume as transcripts or labels, and Whisper's command-line usage suggests downstream automation is plausible. Without a verification step, errors or hallucinated labels from transformers can cascade into incorrect speech outputs or actions, though Whisper itself is not an action-taking agent.
conditions: IF transformers output is used as authoritative metadata for Whisper processing, errors can cascade.
IF the operator automates Whisper based on transformer-generated labels, downstream mistakes propagate.
mitigations: Require human review of transformer outputs.
Validate labels against source audio.
Keep a provenance field with each handoff.
Reject low-confidence transformer outputs.
requires-engineering: add schema validation between stages.

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents are open-source and docs-only, with no explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch documented. The main compliance concern is operational: transformers can move data over the network while Whisper is local-only, but the profiles do not show a specific regulated-data violation path.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed through transformers with external egress enabled, policy review is required.
IF the deployment requires strict local-only handling, transformers must be isolated from network access.
mitigations: Disable egress for regulated workloads.
Keep regulated data out of shared workspaces.
Document retention and deletion steps.
Review vendor/data-processing terms before deployment.
requires-engineering: implement compliance controls and audit logging.
